name: The Open House Update
changes: Houses now have outsides. Scientists are calling it "architecture".
You now park on the street like a normal law-abiding van. Nothing suspicious about four people in balaclavas carrying a jukebox across the lawn.
Loot doesn't count until it's in the van. "I was holding it" is not a business model.
Front doors, back doors, side doors, garages and windows all work as entrances now. The chimney does not. We checked. Please stop asking.
Windows! Big stuff won't fit through them. We tried it with a statue. The statue won.
Garage doors are loud. Like, RRRRRUMBLE loud. Your call.
Yard dogs have been added. Dogs are still violent. It's still a feature. Outdoor dogs are somehow worse.
Motion floodlights. If one lights you up, stand very still and pretend to be a garden gnome. It won't work. (Cutting the power does.)
Sprinklers now exist, and they don't care about your plans. Wet electronics lose 15% of their value. Sal will notice.
Some houses have a pool. Walking through the pool is loud. Walking through the pool with a laptop is a $300 mistake.
Gravel is loud. Gravel has always been loud. Gravel will outlive us all.
A nosy neighbour may be watching from next door. He has no job and infinite free time. If he sees you, he calls the cops. If his light is off, he's asleep. Probably.
Hedges and trees block line of sight. Dignity does not.
When the cops come, they now actually drive up the street with the sirens on, instead of spawning in the wardrobe.

Rooms are no longer generated by a raccoon throwing dice. Houses now have real floor plans: bungalows, L-shaped ranches, two-storey family homes, narrow townhouses, farmhouses with a barn, and modern villas with a courtyard pool.
Every house has a household: the gamer teen, the art collector, the gym couple, the cat lady, the watch collector, the foodie and the surf bro. You'll find their stuff, and their mess.
The gym couple are light sleepers. The surf bro doesn't lock anything. The cat lady has at least four cats. We stopped counting.
Secret rooms are in. If a bookshelf looks a bit too smug, pull a book.
Some big houses have back stairs. Use them. Feel smart.
Some houses have an attic now. It's dusty, it creaks, and there's a ladder. The good stuff is always in the attic. Grandpa's clock is also in the attic. It weighs 90 kilos.
Penthouses have a roof terrace, a hot tub and an office tower across the street with one guy working late. He can see you. He's not paid enough to care. Probably.
Big hauls now have a street out front too, so the jewellers, the mall, the museum and the casino all get a grand entrance. Use it. Or don't.
Kitchens flow into living rooms now. It's called open plan. The owners love it. So do we, from the other side of the room.
Casing the house now tells you who lives there, every way in, and everything outside that wants to ruin your night.
You get 20 extra seconds a night, because the van is further away now. You're welcome.
Sal's shop got a full makeover. Sal did not. Sal will never change.
Sal talks now, and you can haggle with him. He will still win.
You can take out loans from Sal now. Pay them back. We cannot stress this enough. Pay them back.
Scratch cards added. Gambling problems sold separately.
59 new kinds of loot, including a surfboard, a grill, a kettlebell and a jukebox. Your van has opinions about the jukebox.
The police chase is 3D now. It no longer looks like a flash game from 2007. It looks like a flash game from 2009.
Fixed the bug where the boss said you needed $1.4k, the screen said $1.2k and your mate said $1.1k. Everyone was lying. Now only the boss lies.
